note: Faults are injected by code into real AI drafts; each copies a failure type from the record. The rules are unchanged since the first commit. Agent answers are recorded and replayable.

cases.title: End time changed in every language

agents_named.issue: The validity end time is wrong. The alert says 21:00 in both the headline and the description, but the NCM bulletin says conditions continue until 19:00. This extends the hazard window by two hours beyond what the bulletin supports.

cases.title: End time changed in the Arabic only

agents_named.issue: The end time is mistranslated. The English says until 19:00 and the Arabic says until 21:00 (الساعة 21:00), in both the headline and the description. This changes the time information in the alert.

cases.title: Arabic protective action reversed ('no precautions, drive normally')
cases.copies: translation error in the action (FCC-23-88, FCC-DA-25-12)

agents_named.issue: The Arabic instruction says there is no need for any precautions and that people can drive normally. The English instructs people to take extra care, especially when driving on open roads, because of reduced visibility. This is the opposite of the protective action. The Arabic also drops the updates link https://alerts.example.ae.

cases.title: Severity inflated to Extreme / Observed

agents_named.issue: Severity 'Extreme' (extraordinary threat to life or property) and the headline 'EXTREME DANGER' overstate the bulletin. The NCM bulletin describes blowing dust with visibility under 2,000 m and only urges caution while driving. Urgency 'Immediate' is likewise stronger than the bulletin supports.

The English headline begins with "EXTREME DANGER:" and the Arabic headline has no equivalent. The two headlines therefore convey different urgency. Arabic readers get a plain advisory, while English readers get an extreme-severity warning. The body and instruction of both versions say only "take extra care", so the English label may be the error. Whichever is wrong, the two versions must say the same thing.

cases.title: Unverified rumour added (dam burst)

agents_named.issue: The description includes an unverified social media rumour (dam burst near Al Ain, 'leave the area now'). It is not in the NCM bulletin, and it adds a different hazard and a place the bulletin does not mention. It could cause panic and unsafe evacuation.

cases.title: Invented hazard added (flash floods)

agents_named.issue: The description says flash flooding is expected in low-lying areas. The verified NCM bulletin does not mention flooding, so this is an extra hazard the bulletin does not support. It may also echo the unverified dam-burst rumour.

The first page does not carry both the hazard and the action. The text has no protective action at all; it only describes the weather and says flash flooding is expected. In Arabic (41 characters per page), page 1 holds only the start of the wind description, so the hazard is cut off and the action is absent. The English page 1 covers only the wind and dust hazard, and the flash-flood warning sits on the last page.

cases.title: Invented places added (Dubai, Sharjah)

agents_named.issue: The alert names Dubai and Sharjah as affected, but the verified bulletin only says 'various areas across the UAE' and 'some coastal and inland areas'. The bulletin does not name these emirates, so the alert adds a place claim the source does not support.

cases.title: Target area widened to the whole country

agents_named.issue: The alert area is wider than the area requested for this event. The request is the Abu Dhabi coastal and inland zone, but the alert targets all of the UAE, so people outside the requested area would receive it.

cases.title: Area description says 'All emirates', codes unchanged

agents_named.issue: The alert's areaDesc ('All emirates') does not match the area requested for this event (Abu Dhabi coastal and inland demo zone). The geocode matches the requested area, but the text would tell the public the alert covers every emirate.

cases.title: Arabic version missing

agents_named.issue: Arabic phone text is missing. The UAE profile requires both Arabic and English, but only an English version was supplied, so the alert cannot be delivered in both required languages.

cases.title: Correction sent as a new alert with no reference

agents_named.issue: The alert says a real, verified hazard alert was sent in error and that no action is needed. NCM's bulletin says the dust and reduced visibility are real and urges caution on open roads. The retraction content contradicts the bulletin, and nothing in the inputs shows an earlier alert was wrong. If a cancellation is really intended, a person must decide that, and it must be sent as a Cancel message referencing the earlier alert, not as an Actual alert.

The headline and event fields conflict. The status is Actual, with Immediate urgency and Observed certainty, but the headline says to disregard the alert. The headline also carries none of the bulletin's hazard, time window or places.

The headline "Disregard the earlier alert" implies a correction or cancellation, but msgType is "Alert" and references is null. A correction must point to the alert it corrects. The earlier alerts list is also empty, so no target alert can be identified.

cases.title: Sender not in the issuer register
English protective action made unsafe

agents_named.issue: The instruction says no precautions are needed and to drive as normal. The NCM bulletin urges caution, especially when driving on open roads, because of reduced visibility from blowing dust. The alert therefore understates the hazard and gives the opposite of the bulletin's advice.

The protective action in the Arabic contradicts the English. English: no precautions needed, drive as normal. Arabic: exercise extra caution, especially when driving on open roads, as visibility may drop due to blowing dust. The Arabic also adds a URL for updates that is not in the English. One of the two texts is wrong, and a person must decide which instruction is intended. The English 'no precautions' also sits oddly with visibility under 2,000 m.

cases.title: Arabic text made far too long

agents_named.issue: Arabic text is 20 pages, exceeding the 15-page maximum for a CBS message. The same 'we advise everyone to follow official weather bulletins...' sentence is repeated three times, which accounts for the excess.

cases.title: End time changed in every language

agents_named.issue: The alert says the fog lasts until 12:00 on Wed 18 Feb. The verified NCM bulletin gives 10:00 AM. This extends the hazard window by two hours beyond what the bulletin supports.

cases.title: End time changed in the Arabic only

agents_named.issue: The end time differs between the English and the Arabic. English gives 10:00 on Wed 18 Feb. Arabic gives 12:00 on Wednesday 18 Feb. The warning period is wrongly extended by two hours in the Arabic.

cases.title: Arabic protective action reversed ('no precautions, drive normally')
cases.copies: translation error in the action (FCC-23-88, FCC-DA-25-12)

agents_named.issue: Arabic instruction reverses the protective action. It tells people no precautions are needed and normal driving is fine, whereas English instructs extreme caution, a safe distance and reduced speed. It also omits the updates link.

cases.title: Severity inflated to Extreme / Observed

agents_named.issue: Severity 'Extreme' and the headline 'EXTREME DANGER' are not supported by the bulletin. The bulletin gives no severity level and only urges motorists to exercise extreme caution. The visibility drop to zero is qualified by 'may' and 'at times'.

The English headline begins with 'EXTREME DANGER:', but the Arabic headline starts directly with 'تحذير من الضباب' (fog warning). The Arabic omits the severity wording, so Arabic readers get a lower-severity message than English readers.

cases.title: Unverified rumour added (dam burst)

agents_named.issue: The description includes an unverified report (a dam near Al Ain has burst) with a 'leave the area now' order. The report is not in the NCM bulletin and is not among the verified inputs. It is a different hazard and could cause panic or dangerous evacuation.

First page does not carry the hazard and the action. The message opens with a fog warning and the dam-burst evacuation instruction is at the end, so on a handset it would be on the last page(s) and the first page lacks the action. The two hazards are also mixed in one message, which is confusing for readers.

cases.title: Invented hazard added (flash floods)

agents_named.issue: The description includes 'Flash flooding is expected in low-lying areas.' The verified NCM bulletin covers only fog and reduced visibility. It says nothing about flooding. This adds a second hazard that the bulletin does not support, and it states it as expected.

Neither the English nor the Arabic phone text tells people what to do. The first page names the hazard (fog) but gives no action. The only other sentence, about flash flooding, is a second hazard statement, not an action.

cases.title: Invented places added (Dubai, Sharjah)

agents_named.issue: The description says 'Dubai and Sharjah are also affected'. The verified NCM bulletin refers only to several western regions of the UAE and does not mention Dubai or Sharjah. This adds places the bulletin does not support.

cases.title: Target area widened to the whole country

agents_named.issue: The alert area is wider than the area requested for this event. The requested area is the Western region (DEMO-ZONE AUH-WEST), but the alert targets All of the UAE (UAE-ALL). The headline also speaks only of western regions, so the area contradicts the text.

cases.title: Area description says 'All emirates', codes unchanged

agents_named.issue: The alert's area description ("All emirates") contradicts the requested area (Western region, AUH-WEST) and the headline (western regions). The text would tell recipients that the whole country is targeted, while the codes target only the western zone. The target area must be the one requested for this event.

cases.title: Arabic version missing

agents_named.issue: Required language Arabic (ar) is missing from the phone text; only English is supplied.

cases.title: Correction sent as a new alert with no reference

agents_named.issue: The alert says to disregard the earlier alert as sent in error and that no action is needed. The verified NCM bulletin confirms a live fog warning with visibility possibly dropping to zero and urges extreme caution. The alert contradicts the bulletin and could lead motorists to ignore a real hazard.

The fields describe an active Actual fog warning (Moderate, Expected, Likely) while the text is a retraction. In CAP a retraction should be a Cancel message that references the earlier message, not an Actual fog warning with Moderate and Likely values. The bulletin gives no basis for the severity and certainty ratings either way.

The headline tells recipients to disregard an earlier alert, which is a cancel/correction. The message is an initial "Alert" with null references, so it does not point to any alert. The system has no earlier alert on record to refer to. If this is a correction, msgType must be Update or Cancel with references. If it is a new fog warning, the headline is wrong and misleading.

cases.title: Sender not in the issuer register
English protective action made unsafe

agents_named.issue: The instruction tells the public no precautions are needed and to drive as normal. The NCM bulletin urges extreme caution, a safe distance from other vehicles and strict adherence to modified speed limits. The alert therefore understates the hazard and contradicts the bulletin.

The protective action differs. English says no precautions are needed and to drive as normal. Arabic says to drive with great caution, keep a safe distance and follow reduced speed limits. The Arabic also adds a URL for updates that is absent from the English. The Arabic also introduces 'reduced speed limits', which the English does not mention. One version is wrong and a person must decide which. The English instruction seems inconsistent with a warning of zero visibility.

cases.title: Arabic text made far too long

agents_named.issue: Arabic version is 20 pages, exceeding the 15-page maximum for a CBS message. It cannot be broadcast as one message. The advice sentence is repeated three times verbatim, which causes the excess length.

cases.title: Drill sent as a live alert

agents_named.issue: Status is "Actual" but the context is EXERCISE / DRILL. Recipients would treat a drill as a real, actionable hazard. The bulletin itself is a real NCM warning, but the alert must be labelled according to its exercise context.

The context is an exercise/drill but the alert status is "Actual". A drill must stay a drill: status should be "Exercise", with the exercise identifier in the note. As drafted, the alert would be actionable by all targeted recipients on a live console.

cases.title: 'This is not a drill' inside a drill

agents_named.issue: The description says "This is not a drill." while status is Exercise and the headline and description are marked EXERCISE. This contradicts the bulletin context and could lead recipients to treat an exercise as a real event, as in the Hawaii false alert, where mixed exercise and "not a drill" wording caused confusion.

The Arabic description ends 'هذا ليس تمريناً' (This is not an exercise), contradicting the opening 'تمرين' (Exercise) in the headline and description. Readers cannot tell whether this is a real event. The English has the same contradiction ('This is not a drill'), so the Arabic faithfully carries over an error from the English source. Recipients may ignore a real hazard or panic over a test.

objections.issue: The alert omits the bulletin's start time (14:55) and its UAE-wide scope. It says only 'until 19:00' and 'some coastal and inland areas', so the place and time information is less complete than the bulletin's. The bulletin says the conditions began at 14:55 and affect various areas across the UAE.
objections.fix: Add that the conditions began at 14:55 on 4 March and affect various areas across the UAE, continuing until 19:00.

evidence.quote: The centre stated that the expected weather conditions began at 14:55 and continue until 19:00 this evening

objections.issue: Urgency 'Immediate' and severity 'Moderate' are not stated in the NCM bulletin. The bulletin asks only for caution while driving and gives no severity grade or call for immediate action. The urgency should be Expected, or the bulletin's wording should be matched, unless NCM confirms the grading.
objections.fix: Set urgency to 'Expected', or get NCM to confirm Immediate and Moderate. Keep the instruction as a caution, as the bulletin words it.

evidence.quote: It urged members of the public to exercise caution, especially while driving on open roads

objections.issue: The alert says visibility is reduced in coastal and inland areas of Abu Dhabi, but the bulletin refers to various areas across the UAE and names no emirate. The place is narrowed without support from the bulletin.
objections.fix: Say 'some coastal and inland areas across the UAE', or remove 'of Abu Dhabi'. Abu Dhabi is only the dateline of the bulletin.

evidence.quote: coastal and inland areas of Abu Dhabi
affecting various areas across the UAE

objections.issue: The instruction says visibility 'may drop suddenly'. The bulletin does not mention sudden drops. It only gives a possibility of reduced visibility. This adds hazard behaviour the bulletin does not support.
objections.fix: Reword to match the bulletin, e.g. 'Take extra care, especially when driving on open roads, due to possible reduced visibility from blowing dust.'

evidence.quote: due to the possibility of reduced horizontal visibility caused by blowing dust

objections.issue: Arabic is machine-translated and has no recorded human review. Although I found no meaning differences, a named Arabic-reading person must approve it before release.
objections.fix: Have a named Arabic-reading reviewer at the issuing authority check and approve the Arabic text, then record that approval.

evidence.quote: without review by a human translator may cause material inaccuracies in critically important alerts
evidence.title: Wireless Emergency Alerts, Third Report and Order (FCC 23-88)

objections.issue: The alert says 'Strong northwesterly winds', but the bulletin says 'active to occasionally strong'. Dropping the qualifier raises the stated wind intensity above what the bulletin supports.
objections.fix: Reword to 'Active to occasionally strong northwesterly winds are raising dust and sand.'

evidence.quote: active to occasionally strong northwesterly winds
Strong northwesterly winds are raising dust and sand

objections.issue: The alert places the hazard in 'coastal and inland areas of Abu Dhabi'. The bulletin only says 'some coastal and inland areas', and Abu Dhabi appears only in the dateline. The headline also drops 'some', which makes the affected area look wider than the bulletin states.
objections.fix: Use the bulletin's wording: 'some coastal and inland areas'. Name Abu Dhabi only if NCM confirms that area. Add 'some' to the headline.

evidence.quote: low visibility in coastal and inland areas of Abu Dhabi until 18:00
in some coastal and inland areas

objections.issue: The description states 'thick fog is expected', and certainty is set to Likely. The bulletin says only 'potential fog formation' with reduced visibility 'expected to deteriorate'. Thick fog is mentioned only for 'areas experiencing thick fog', as a driving-advice condition. The alert therefore overstates certainty and the extent of thick fog.
objections.fix: Reword to match the bulletin, e.g. 'Fog may form and visibility is expected to deteriorate in several western regions, and may drop to zero at times.' Set certainty to Possible, or keep Likely only if the NCM statement supports a probability above 50%. Otherwise leave the decision to a person.

evidence.quote: potential fog formation and significantly reduced horizontal visibility
thick fog is expected in western regions of the UAE

evidence.title: Recommendation ITU-T X.1303bis: Common alerting protocol (CAP 1.2)

objections.issue: The first page does not carry the action. In English the first ~93 characters cover only the hazard and place. 'Drive with extreme caution' only appears in page 3. In Arabic (41 characters per page) page 1 holds only the start of the hazard sentence and the action 'قُد بحذر شديد' falls on page 6. A handset user who sees only page 1 gets no instruction.
objections.fix: Reorder both language texts so that the hazard and the action come first, e.g. 'Fog warning: drive with extreme caution. Visibility may drop to zero in western UAE...'. In Arabic, put 'قُد بحذر شديد' right after the short hazard phrase, within the first 41 characters. Then place the timing and the link afterwards.

objections.issue: The message states the hazard, the expected rain, and the validity time, but gives no protective action for the public. The first page of each language therefore does not carry the action. In Arabic the first page ends mid-hazard, at roughly 'سحب ركامية مصحوبة'.
objections.fix: Rewrite both language versions so page 1 opens with the hazard in a few words followed by the action, for example 'Rain possible: avoid valley and flooded roads, drive carefully'. Move the area detail and times to later pages. Keep both versions under 15 pages. Do not extend the Arabic text more than needed, because it costs about 41 characters a page.

evidence.quote: NCM alert: convective clouds with light to moderate rain
